workedExamples.question: In the diagram the two horizontal lines are parallel and the transversal meets them at $P$ and $Q$. The angle at $P$ below the top line and to the left of the transversal is $58^\circ$. Find the angles marked $x$ and $y$ at $Q$, giving reasons. (Not drawn to scale.)
workedExamples.solution:
**Angle $x$:** it lies between the parallel lines, on the opposite side of the transversal from the $58^\circ$ angle. They form a Z-shape, so
$$x = 58^\circ \quad \text{(alternate angles are equal)}$$

**Angle $y$:** it lies between the parallel lines, on the same side of the transversal as the $58^\circ$ angle, so the pair is co-interior:
$$y = 180^\circ - 58^\circ = 122^\circ \quad \text{(co-interior angles add up to } 180^\circ\text{)}$$

Check: $x$ and $y$ lie on a straight line at $Q$, and $58^\circ + 122^\circ = 180^\circ$.
